name: Isthmus Town
description: A former logging town, currently squeaking by largely on profits made from fishing West Lake. Fewer than thirty families call it home. The town market runs from 8am to 2pm each day and carries any items under 10gp (see Marketplace in the 2e Player's Guide). Local specialties are fried cod, roasted frog legs, and hot stewberry pie. Fishing equipment (15gp), bog shoes (10gp a pair), and rainproof clothing (15gp) are popular. Factions: the Tideborn, a hierarchical religious sect that worships Rivulus, a petty god of rivers and lakes; its initiation is a ritual drowning that occasionally kills participants, and survivors take a water-related name (Carp, Reed, Oxbow, and so on). The Order of Nine, a consortium of merchants, scholars, and the very powerful, focused on the discovery, identification, and regulation of Relics; it now focuses on the Roots and pays handsomely for information regarding Gates. Route: the module gives no road into Isthmus Town itself; the Farming Path runs South out of it, through the Humpbacks and into the Cities beyond.

name: The Stuffed Inn
description: The only tavern in Isthmus Town, and the only place for travelers to safely rest. A night in a shared room is 10gp, including an onion soup and weak beer. Attached stables offer basic boarding for 5gp per night. The Inn is owned by Reeve Trellis; most of the real work is performed by Drum and a local cook. Outside: the building is H-shaped, with its main entrance on the northeast corner. On the east side is a small trapdoor, chained to the ground and openable only from inside unless the chain is broken; it is in direct view of the Butcher Shop's second-floor window, and there are footsteps in the dirt nearby. On the west side is the stable: four exposed stalls, empty save one holding a single horse and wagon belonging to Jandy, both bearing the livery of the Cities. Drum manages the stables, but only checks in on the lodging once per day. Inside: the tavern is small, with only three tables arranged perpendicular to the bar. Guest rooms are all on the second floor, reached by a single flight of stairs on the south side. A small office tucked in the corner is nearly always locked (only Reeve Trellis has the key) but is easily picked. The tavern is functionally closed until 3pm, when Drum and the cook arrive to clean up and prepare food. Route: in Isthmus Town, with the Butcher Shop beside it across an alley; the Reeve's Office is in the back of the Inn.

name: The Reeve's Office
description: A dank, uncomfortable room in the back of the Stuffed Inn, empty save for a single desk and a locked cellar door. Desk: a single drawer. Inside is a small black book, a fake tithing record. Comparing it to the true record in the basement, or its twin in Jandy's satchel, can prove that the Reeve has been stealing from the tithe owed to the Cities. Cellar door: locked; both Reeve Trellis and Drum have keys. Route: in the back of the Stuffed Inn, reached through the Inn's office; its cellar door is locked.

name: Cellar
description: A small, dank space filled with various crates; the air is heavy with the scent of damp earth. Crates: clothing, household items, and food, marked for the tithe of one of the great cities. They are meant for Jandy, who failed to retrieve them a week ago. Workbench: a workbench containing various tools leans against one wall. It has a false drawer hidden underneath, holding the town's true tithing ledger. Comparing it to the fake ledger in the Reeve's office upstairs, or its twin in Jandy's satchel, can prove that the Reeve has been stealing from the tithe owed to the Cities. Trapdoor: a trapdoor and ladder in the ceiling of the southeast corner lead up into the alley between the Inn and the Butcher. A thick chain is looped through it and held together with a large brass lock; only Reeve Trellis has the key. Route: entered from the Reeve's Office (the cellar door there is locked); its trapdoor in the SE corner opens into the alley between the Stuffed Inn and the Butcher Shop.

name: Butcher Shop
description: A rustic two-story building adjacent to the Stuffed Inn. A headless chicken is painted on the north entrance. The first floor has no windows; the second has two on each of the four sides. An alley separates the shop from the east wing of the Stuffed Inn. First floor: the floor is gritty with wood chips and feathers. A large, bloody butcher block divides the space. A flight of stairs in the southwest corner leads to the second floor. Flavia is here all day. Butcher block: a hidden compartment, triggered by a latch underneath, holds the day's current earnings ([1d20] x the hour of the day). The money is taken out each evening and locked in the desk upstairs. Second floor: eight windows (two in each cardinal direction) covered by fine window dressing. A four-poster bed dominates the northeast corner. South windows show the town square and a view of the Farming Path. Bed: underneath is a small dagger ([d6]) with a gold hilt, worth 20gp. Desk: paperwork and writing implements; a single drawer, locked. Sitting at the desk gives ample view of the alley between the Stuffed Inn and the Butcher, including the cellar exit there. Flavia keeps the drawer key on a chain around her neck. Inside are a sales ledger (half-finished, just as Flavia found it on the desk the night Aldra went missing) and 870gp. Painting: a humanoid creature (Rivulus) rising from the waters, wearing a white robe with three squiggly lines cut into the front. Flavia will say it was purchased only a few months ago at great expense. Worth 400gp. Route: in Isthmus Town, adjacent to the Stuffed Inn with an alley between them.

name: Giva's Home
description: A single-room shack on the north side of town, built from wood more weathered and older than the wood used in other buildings in town. Door: painted bright purple, recently. Giva believes the paint protects against evil spirits. Dried vegetation stuffed into the top of the door (dried wolfsbane and other herbs) wards off werewolves. Interior: a heated wood stove dominates the west wall, and a small bed is tucked beneath a window on the north side. In the kitchen, a table is set with two glasses and a wine bottle: a very old vintage, worth 50gp. Giva says she sets out the wine "for company," and makes it very clear the party is not who she is waiting for. She will admit that the person she is waiting on (Jandy) missed their last rendezvous; he was meant to stop by on his way out of town nearly a week ago. Route: in Isthmus Town, on the north side of town.

name: Farming Path
description: A dry, well-trod footpath stretching South from Isthmus Town and through the Humpbacks, and into the Cities beyond. Small farms and independent homesteads are scattered alongside it. A small trail splits off to Dunston and East Lake Pass. Route: from Isthmus Town, the Farming Path runs South through the Humpbacks and into the Cities beyond; a small trail splits off it to Dunston and East Lake Pass.

name: Dunston
description: A thin circle of ramshackle homes built far apart from one another. Originally a fishing village, before the water in East Lake turned sour; only impoverished fishers and unlucky farmers make their home here now. Connects to East Lake Pass. Route: a small trail splits off the Farming Path to Dunston, which connects to East Lake Pass.

name: Fasha's Farm
description: On the West end of the Dunston circle is a frail, decrepit farmhouse. It sits adjacent to a broken corral on one side and a withered field on the other. Corral: three sheep graze in the half-broken corral, their water troughs nearly empty. Fields: decaying crops and unirrigated dirt; they look as if no one has tended them for months. Farmhouse: a single-room hovel containing an ice-box, a moldering bed, and a small wood stove. The floor is muddy and covered in reeds and other small grasses. Ice-box: empty and clearly unused for a long time. Bed: long animal hairs line the sweat-stained sheets. Stove: a small box is buried beneath the ashes, containing 130gp and a Tideborn pendant worth 25gp that once belonged to Aldra. Reeds: Fasha brought them in from the Downs after leaving Aldra's body at Bone Sump. Route: on the West end of the Dunston circle.

name: Abandoned Home
description: A dilapidated home on the southeast end of the Dunston circle. Half the roof has caved in, and a wide woven tarp is draped across where the south wall should be. Inside: completely bare and lacking any furniture; the floorboards look brand new. Floorboards: Fasha (with the help of the Reeve) hired workers to renovate the home. The flooring is nearly finished, but an imperfect section in the southwest corner is still accessible, where a single person could climb in halfway. Underneath the floorboards are two large sacks, Fasha's cut of the tithe, worth 200gp each. Removing them would take time and draw considerable attention during the day. Route: on the southeast end of the Dunston circle.

name: Old Mill Road
description: A short dirt path connecting Isthmus Town to the Stone Forest, where it quickly disappears. Deadmill is visible through the trees, just at the edge of the wood. If Annafranax has returned, the grove and the mill will be gone, replaced by a massive sinkhole. See "If the Gate has Opened...". Route: a short dirt path leads from Isthmus Town to the edge of the Stone Forest, where it disappears.

name: The Stone Forest
description: An unending wood stretching far to the north, its vast expanse halted only by the Marble Sea. For centuries the forest's lumber fed the needs of the Cities, until the allure of gems and ore drew their insatiable hunger South. A small creek flows from the border of the wood, northeast of East Lake, before terminating at Bone Sump. Entering the Stone Forest after dark, creating a loud disturbance, or stepping off the path triggers a roll on the Wilderness Events table (see Player's Guide pg. 78). A common arboreal predator here is the Night Cat (statblock 2.1), a nocturnal marsupial that hunts in packs. The only warning before they strike is a tick-tick-tick from the boughs above as they coordinate their attack; they go after whoever is last in the marching order. The target must make a DEX save or take damage directly to STR. Despite their name, Night Cats will attack targets during the day as well. This region will be explored in greater detail in future adventures in this series. Route: Old Mill Road leads to its edge and disappears there; the forest stretches north to the Marble Sea.

name: Deadmill
description: An old gristmill at the outskirts of the forest, shrouded by overgrown arboreal pillars. Due to the grove's near-constant darkness, local teens believe it is haunted. (It's not.) The mill is half-sunk into the ground, with large paddles protruding from the north side above a dried-up riverbed. Anyone coming from Old Mill Road arrives at the south entrance. Ground: the structure is slowly sinking, and some of the ground has the properties of quicksand. The south entrance is unsafe: DEX save to escape; a failed save causes the victim to sink even further (max 3 attempts). Paddles: mostly obscured from the south, save for the tip of one, painted a bright, unfaded white (see 2. The Waterwheel). Time loop: every 30 seconds the mill door opens and a man (Jandy) steps out. He quickly looks back as if hearing something, shrugs, turns around, and falls to his death in the quicksand. The sound he hears is the device being recharged after its last loop. The loop can be broken either by saving Jandy or by freeing the Relic from the stone and taking it a short distance away. Route: anyone coming from Old Mill Road arrives at the building's south entrance.

name: 1. Interior
description: A large millstone occupies most of the room, attached to some metallic machinery. A small leather satchel leans against the south wall. The building is slowly sinking. Millstone: a search reveals something metallic and glowing beneath the stone. The Echo Spark is stuck in a loop, held by the weight of the millstone and Jandy's continual deaths; its charge is restored, then depleted, over and over. Machinery: the wooden lever that turns the stone has rotted away, so the grindstone cannot be turned with this device. Satchel (belongs to Jandy): contains a dagger ([d6]), a notebook, a tithing record, Rations (2 uses left), a Torch (3 uses), and 23gp. Notebook: a short history of the region, snippets of interviews with Giva, and a section called "The Lumber Trade, a History." Tithing record: a discrepancy exists between this copy and its twin in the basement of the Stuffed Inn. Sinking: the south side has sunk halfway into the ground. If more than three people (including Jandy) are inside the mill at the same time, it fully sinks into the earth (DEX save to escape or accomplish anything of note). Route: inside Deadmill, entered through its south entrance; the module gives no separate path to this room.

name: 2. The Waterwheel
description: A pair of sturdy water wheel paddles sit motionless. The riverbed is completely dry and full of deadleaves and other detritus. Paddles: show no signs of rot, their paint as white as the day they were painted. Investigation reveals an unusual script carved into both paddles. Script: an archaic phrase that only Giva, Jandy, or a person learned in ancient texts could decode. It says, "To prime, turn counter-clockwise." Pushing the paddles manually turns the millstone inside just enough to pull out the Relic from underneath; this requires at least two able-bodied people. Leaves: partially hidden in the debris and dried humus is a well-preserved portable iron cage. The cage is a Wisp Lamp, in which Annafranax has trapped a Wisp. It has been here for more than a week, absorbing the many deaths of Jandy, and has grown so large that the cage is nearly too small for it. Contact with iron is quite painful for Wisps, and it is in near-constant agony as a result. It wishes only for freedom, and its revenge. If freed before Annafranax returns, it flies directly to the witch's home, leaving a trail of fire in the wake of its vengeance. Route: inside Deadmill; the module gives no separate path to the waterwheel beyond the mill's interior.

name: East Lake Pass
description: A lakeside path, overgrown with shrubs and wet grasses. Winds along East Lake and through the Downs, then west toward Old Mill Road. Route: a lakeside path reached from Dunston or the trail off the Farming Path; it winds along East Lake and through the Downs, then west toward Old Mill Road.

name: The Downs
description: A muddy, stinking bog shrouded in mist, and a popular source for horror stories (all untrue). The only creatures that live here are frogs, fish, and birds. Its deposits of mud and stink are home to a multitude of corpses, both of animals and of those who left the trail. Parties traveling on foot add a Fatigue. Route: along East Lake Pass, through the muddy bog; parties on foot add a Fatigue.

name: White Tower Fens
description: A small wood East of the Downs, named for its ruined white tower, shrouded in the mists of the nearby bog. Entry is via East Lake Pass at the fork toward Old Mill Road. Route: via East Lake Pass at the fork toward Old Mill Road, East of the Downs.

name: 1. Whistlewood
description: An almost invisible wire crosses the path, tied between two trees. If broken, it emits a high-pitched sound only animals can hear. Route: on the path through White Tower Fens, the first of its three traps.

name: 2. Pit Trap
description: Hidden beneath a carpet of leaves and debris is a small pit, its bottom lined with sharp wooden stakes (d6 STR damage). Route: on the path through White Tower Fens, the second of its three traps.

name: 3. Log Trap
description: A small log is stretched across a small creek, offering an easy crossing. When weight is applied in the center, the log rotates, loudly dumping the victim into the creek below, which is teeming with spinemoss. Spinemoss: contains a numbing toxin. Contact with skin leaves the victim deprived and their attacks impaired for [1d4-1] hours. Route: on the path through White Tower Fens, the third trap, where the path crosses a small creek.

name: The White Tower
description: A broken tower 40ft high, colored white as snow. A thick ladder stands against the tower's side. The upper portion of the tower is completely missing. Up The Ladder: the tower's bottom is bathed in darkness, its smooth white walls glittering in the light. No plant matter grows inside. Bottom: a viscous, amber-colored liquid creating a pool four feet deep, filling the tower's base. Liquid: an acid that only harms flesh (4 STR damage on contact). Any other material placed in it is undamaged and, if fully immersed, perfectly preserved. The substance is highly flammable, burning away completely within a few moments and leaving its contents unharmed. Shine: something shines inside. It is an armored skeleton from a time long ago, still wearing perfectly preserved chainmail. On its belt is a bag of ancient gold pieces (82gp) and a torn silk rope (42ft). Glittering: residue from the acid at the bottom of the tower. Oily to the touch, it sting like nettles (as printed). Route: the module names White Tower Fens for its ruined white tower, so the tower is reached through the Fens, entered via East Lake Pass at the fork toward Old Mill Road.

name: Bone Sump
description: The creek terminates in a small bog a few minutes' walk south of White Tower Fens. A smell of rot and decay permeates the area. The area does not appear on any maps and is known only to Fasha and Giva. Route: stairs under the mound lead down into the Temple of the Fungal Lizards, the only way in. Smell: animals caught in the bog's sticky solution quickly succumb to drowning or starvation; many corpses lie here in varying states of decay. Aldra's body is among them, floating amongst the reeds, well-preserved by the bog's unique chemistry. His chest is torn open and the heart has been removed. Mound: on the west end of the bog, a large mound of grass and detritus that appears freshly made. Pushing the detritus aside reveals stairs leading down into the earth beneath the bog. This is the entry to the Temple of the Fungal Lizards; the stairwell smells earthy and slightly floral. Two sconces are installed at eye-level on the walls inside the stairwell, each with a diamond-shaped object inserted. The objects can be removed and are valuable (150gp each, bulky). They are lights controlled from T7 (Light Room) and are presently turned off. The player learns of Bone Sump only from Fasha or Giva; until then it is not known to them, so do not send the player there. When Fasha or Giva tells the player of it, call discover_location for bone-sump.

name: Temple of the Fungal Lizards
description: A dark complex, built as a building-sized ship shaped like a beetle; its entry, reached by the stairs under the Bone Sump mound, is the beetle's "head." Route: the Chamber of Worship (T9) lies deeper in the temple, and a short hallway runs from it to the door at T10a. General information: no light. Sconces with diamond-shaped objects protrude from the corners of each room (see T7, Light Room); they are currently off. The walls and floors are painted blue-black and made from a foreign alloy. They cannot be chipped or broken by mundane weapons, although fire and explosive powders have some effect. Two Surarus roam the temple. They appear on both Encounters and Environmental results from the Cairn 2e Dungeon Events table (in the rule set: cairn2e, table "Dungeon Events").

name: T1. Antechamber
description: Small chambers have been carved into both the east and west walls, each with a single waist-high pedestal installed. Small statues have been fused onto all but the southeast corner, which remains empty. Statues: each can be twisted off, but makes a very loud noise. Each is worth 50gp. NW statue: a bulbous cluster of eggs, held by a scaled hand. SW statue: a cluster of fungal spores growing from a salt-like pillar. NE statue: a large, veiny spore; the outline of something reptilian is visible within. SE statue: a copper-like ring is all that is left of whatever once sat here. Route: the module does not say which room the Bone Sump mound stairs open into; the Antechamber is the temple's first room, entered from the stairs under the mound.

name: T2. Columbarium
description: A thin hall divides the room, with chambers built into each side. On the north side are stacks of paper products; on the south side, rows of chipped pottery. On the southwest wall, two large horizontal seams are arranged in parallel a few feet apart. Paper: useless withered scrolls and eggshell fragments are piled together. Buried beneath them is a small tube of scaled leather, stuffed with a Watersnatch (see below). Pottery: ancient urns arranged in stacks. It takes at least two turns to search them all (characters can split up the work). A pot in the first row holds the mummified remains of a fragile, bird-like creature, valuable only to specialty buyers (150gp). In the back is a nondescript urn, firmly attached to the chamber; twisting its top opens the hatch to T4 but creates a very loud noise (roll on the Dungeon Events table). Seams: a hatch to T4. The seams are too narrow for a crowbar or blade, and there are no obvious handles, buttons, or levers in sight. Watersnatch (item, printed in T2): a cylindrical object that can absorb up to a wagon's load of water (or roughly 1000 gallons). 1 Charge. Recharge: remove from moisture of any kind for a month and a day. Route: the module gives no direct link from the temple's entry; the urn in the back of the room, if twisted (very loud), opens a hatch to T4, and its seams also open a hatch to T4.

name: T3. Breeding Chamber
description: Enormous fungal growths sprout from three sacs scattered across the floor. All but one have burst, leaving large gaping holes. A fourth nodule sits intact. Fungus: embryonic chambers for the Suraru. A learned person would note that they appear to have burst weeks ago. Nodule: twice the size of the others, pulsating and radiating a thin heat. It contains a fully-grown Suraru, ready to hatch. The sac will burst open if a loud noise is made nearby, or on an Encounter roll on the Dungeon Events table. If woken, it attacks any creature in sight, as hatchlings often eat their unhatched siblings. Route: the module does not say how to reach this place from the others; it is reached through its parent or story.

name: T4. Maintenance Tunnel
description: Grey, barren corridors connecting T2 to T6 and T7. U-shaped bars extend from the terminus of each hallway; twisted, they open a hatch to each. In the central corridor, a long cloth is covered by some rubble. Cloth: among the debris is a very well-preserved skeleton of a tall, bird-like humanoid with a small red crest on its head. Its throat is ripped open, and it is wrapped in Moon Cloth. It carries a small Curved Dagger (d6) with a red jewel on it. Route: corridors connect it to T2, T6, and T7; U-shaped bars open a hatch at each end.

name: T5. Hall of Glyphs
description: The East wall overflows with intricate carvings, read from topmost to bottom: (1) humanoid figures stand on a tower, pointing toward an object falling from the sky that looks like an enormous beetle; (2) tall, winged figures wearing enormous headdresses stream out of a hole at the front of the "beetle," followed by a pair of crouched, lizard-like creatures; (3) the lizard-like creatures rip apart the humanoid onlookers and overwhelm the tower; (4) the winged figures stand above a crowd of kneeling humanoids, their lizard "pets" standing aside. Route: the module does not say how to reach this place from the others; it is reached through its parent or story.

name: T6. Waste Disposal
description: In the center of this square-shaped room is a square well, waist-high. Well: hundreds of feet deep. A light source reveals ancient refuse floating in the water at the bottom. Three nozzles protrude from the south wall, with no visible controls in sight; a drain and grate are installed beneath each. Nozzles: automatic showers that spray scalding hot water whenever weight is placed on their drain. A single chirp from a corner light sconce is the only warning. Drains: pulling up the grate in the southwest corner triggers a hatch in the west wall, opening a secret door to T4. Seams: on the west wall, two large horizontal seams are arranged in parallel a few feet apart. They are a hatch to T4; like those in T2 and T7, they are too narrow for a crowbar or blade, and there are no obvious handles, buttons, or levers in sight. Route: from T4 (Maintenance Tunnel), through a hatch at its seams or a secret door in the west wall opened by the SW grate.

name: T7. Light Room
description: This room smells like ozone. At the east exit, a small pad is installed in the wall at shoulder height. A diamond-shaped board is built into the north wall. On the west wall, two large horizontal seams are arranged in parallel a few feet apart. The layout allows a clear view of T8 and the fungal growth in T9. Forcefield: an invisible forcefield between T7 and T8 causes only a minor shock on contact, but cannot be penetrated by any normal means. Pad: controls the forcefield between T7 and T8. There is no other way of shutting it off, save disconnecting the control board. Board: a dial on the board controls the light sconces in each room. If turned to extreme brightness, the diamond-shaped bulbs in every room will explode after one dungeon cycle ([d4] STR damage to anyone nearby). Three immediate chirps from each sconce are the only warning. All nearby Surarus will come directly to T7 immediately after. The board can be removed, but all wall sconces and the forcefield will then be permanently disabled. The board would be very valuable to an Aurifex or like-minded profession (500gp). A small switch underneath the board activates a secret door to T4 in the west wall. Seams: a hatch to T4; like those in T2 and T6, they are too narrow for a crowbar or blade, and there are no obvious handles, buttons, or levers in sight. Route: from T4, through a hatch at its seams or a secret door in the west wall opened by a switch under the board; its east exit leads toward the forcefield to T8.

name: T8. Preparation Room
description: This room smells faintly like ozone. It is completely bare, save for a grate in the floor and an enormous nozzle in the ceiling. The layout allows a clear view of T7 and the fungal growth in T9. Forcefield: an invisible forcefield in the hall between T7 and T8 causes only a minor shock on contact and cannot be penetrated by any normal means. It can only be disabled in T7. Nozzle: activates automatically when any weight is placed on the grate, spraying a massive gush of superheated water (3 STR damage). A single chirp from a corner light sconce is the only warning. Route: east of T7, across the forcefield in the hall between them, which can only be disabled from T7; the growth in T9 completely blocks T9's west exit to T8.

name: T9. Chamber of Worship
description: The room smells like a slaughterhouse, and streaks of blood and viscera are strewn across the floor. A short hallway leads from this room to the door at T10a. An enormous fungal chamber grows in the southwest corner. Two Surarus are here. Gore: the remains of Fasha's previous victims (except Aldra) are all here. Each body is missing its heart, made clear by a deep wound in the chest. Depending on the day (see p.3), there may be one potential victim still living, tied up and unconscious. Surarus: sleeping, eating, and placing large chunks of flesh in a pile near the fungal growth. If one is killed, the others will attempt to wake the Imperator by slashing open its sac. Growth: a Suraru Imperator. The west exit to T8 is completely blocked by the growth. Route: the west exit to T8 is completely blocked by the growth, so the module's remaining link is the short hallway that runs from T9 to the T10a door.

name: T10a. Interrogation Room Door
description: A short hallway connects T9 to a large metallic door. A single hooked gash is cut into the right-hand side, and a small window is built into the door six feet from the ground. A metallic handle is adjacent to the door (left, facing the door). Door: normally opened only by slotting the Curved Dagger from T4 into the gash. Window: reveals the room's contents in their entirety. Thick but breakable glass. Handle: opens a drawer, similar to a mail slot. It is slick with blood. Viscera in T10b are dropped through this drawer. Route: a short hallway leads from T9 to this metal door, which normally opens only when the Curved Dagger from T4 is slotted into the gash.

name: T10b. Interrogation Room (Interior)
description: Reached only through the door at T10a, from the hallway off T9. Adjacent to the door (right, facing the hall) is a small slot above some blood and viscera. Two chains dangle from the ceiling in the center, just above a dark stoneblock jutting from the floor. If Vuk has not yet returned to full form, a swirling cloud of ash slowly circles the room. Viscera: hearts from Vuk's victims, belonging to Fasha's victims, dropped through the drawer in T10a. If the drawer outside the room is open, this one closes. See Vuk to determine how many are here (there should be at least one). Block: a small crack is visible on one side and can be broken after a few minutes of smashing. Inside is a large blue memory prism (bulky, worth 1000gp). Cloud: Vuk, now an ash phantom, not the Lich Queen. She was raised to unlife by the exposure of her decaying flesh to the memory prism, and she cannot leave the room until she has consumed three human hearts. She cannot return to her full form until she has consumed three hearts and the door at T10a has been opened. She is not the Lich Queen until then. At the start of the adventure, she has already consumed Aldra's heart, leaving only two remaining. Until then, she is trapped in T10b. If the party arrives within 24 hours of her transformation, she will have broken free of her prison and can be found at T9. Route: behind the metal door at T10a, which normally opens only when the Curved Dagger from T4 is slotted into the gash; the module gives no other entry.
